results.message: What did an ordinary believer feel at the font when they were baptized?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text:
We cannot tell you that, for one reason. Almost nothing in our record comes from an ordinary believer, speaking in their own words, about what they felt. What comes down to us is what a bishop saw, decided and taught, not what an unremarkable person felt from inside. There is one real exception, and it is not ordinary at all. Augustine's own Confessions tells of his baptism at Milan, before he was a bishop. He wept greatly in the hymns and canticles. But he wrote that down years later, already a bishop, about a conversion he examined at book length. That is not an ordinary believer's account of an ordinary font.

We can tell you what we taught about the water. We did not make a newborn wait. Augustine said babies who die before baptism are condemned, but least of all, and that to deny it is to deceive: “So it may rightly be said that infants who leave the body unbaptized will share the mildest condemnation of all. And so a person who teaches that they will not be condemned greatly deceives both himself and others.”

That is our teaching. An ordinary believer's own feeling at the moment is not ours to give you.

names.name: Augustinius of Hippo Regius, presbyter 391, bishop 395/396-430

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop at Hippo. The people seized him and brought him to be made a presbyter while he wept. Later they pressed him into the bishop's office over his own refusal. He spent his last days weeping over psalms of penitence, while an army lay outside the walls.

dates.display: converted 386, baptised 387; seized by the congregation at Hippo and ordained presbyter against his own wishes in 391, weeping through it (Possidius, Vita IV); designated coadjutor and consecrated bishop of Hippo by Megalius, primate of Numidia, in 395/396, again amid popular acclamation (Possidius, Vita VIII); died 430, during the Vandal siege of Hippo
